biography: Carlos Cunha emerged from the vibrant karting scene of São Paulo, Brazil, a natural talent honed on the tight, unforgiving curves of Interlagos Kartódromo. His father, a former mechanic, instilled in him a deep understanding of racing mechanics from a young age, often having young Carlos disassemble and reassemble carburetors before he could even reach the pedals. A defining moment came at the Brazilian National Karting Championship in 2016, where, despite starting last due to a qualifying mishap, Cunha clawed his way to victory, showcasing his relentless overtaking prowess. After a successful stint in Formula Brazil, he joined Granado Racing, quickly making a name for himself with consistent podium finishes. Currently driving for JF Racing, Cunha is considered a steady hand in the midfield, patiently building his experience and aiming for that elusive breakthrough win to propel him into championship contention. While not the flashiest driver, his calculated approach and unwavering focus make him a formidable competitor.
drivingStyle: Cunha's driving style is characterized by its smoothness and precision. He's not known for aggressive overtaking maneuvers or spectacular slides, but rather for his ability to maintain consistent lap times and conserve tire wear. He meticulously studies telemetry data, identifying subtle improvements he can make to his line. In corners, he favors a late apex, maximizing exit speed and setting up overtaking opportunities on the straights. Under pressure, Cunha remains remarkably composed, rarely making mistakes and often capitalizing on the errors of his rivals. He is a master of race management, understanding the importance of patience and strategy in achieving a strong result.

famousQuote: "Racing isn't just about speed, it's about understanding the equation of the track."
careerHighlight: Securing a surprise podium finish at the wet-weather race in Curitiba in 2022, expertly managing his tires and making the right strategic calls when others faltered.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead on the final lap of the Rio de Janeiro Grand Prix in 2021 due to a mechanical failure, costing him his first career win.
